parts.label: i(ii)
parts.technique: Impulse-momentum / collision (Newton's law of impact / PCLM)
parts.reason: This question requires impulse-momentum equations for a direct collision between two particles. No M-statement mentions momentum, impulse, or collisions (M6-M9 cover units, kinematics, forces/Newton's laws, moments only) - this concept is entirely absent from the listed statements, so it is out of spec even though the underlying algebra is simple.

parts.label: (a)(i)(ii)
parts.technique: Moments of forces on a rigid rod with two supports
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers moments in simple static contexts, including problems with parallel coplanar forces on a rigid rod (beam on two supports is a standard example).

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Extension of the same moments problem, still within M9.1's scope of simple static moment problems.

parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers interpreting/sketching velocity-time graphs including gradient and area under graph.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: M7.3 covers use and derivation of constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion; forming and solving simultaneous/quadratic equations from suvat is standard application.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces perpendicular to inclined plane, friction force
parts.reason: M8.6 covers the F≤μR friction model and M8.2 guidance explicitly extends to resolving forces on an inclined plane.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law on inclined plane with friction, suvat for distance
parts.reason: M8.2/M8.6 cover resolving on inclined plane with friction and Newton's second law; M7.3 covers suvat to find distance travelled.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law down the plane with friction, suvat for speed
parts.reason: Same combination of resolving forces on inclined plane, friction, and constant acceleration formulae, all covered by M8.2/M8.6/M7.3.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Vectors - finding velocity and speed (magnitude) from position vectors
parts.reason: P10.2/P10.4 cover magnitude of vectors and position vectors; M7.3 extends suvat to 2D vectors, so finding velocity from displacement and its magnitude (speed) is in spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Position vector as function of time using r = r0 + vt
parts.reason: M7.3 guidance explicitly covers suvat in 2D using vectors, e.g. r = ut + ... in i-j form, matching this show-that.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Parallel vectors condition (ratio of components equal)
parts.reason: P10.3 covers parallel vectors as part of vector algebra, directly applicable to solving for t when one vector is parallel to another.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Equating position vectors of two particles to find meeting point
parts.reason: This uses position vectors and vector algebra (P10.4) together with 2D kinematics (M7.3); it is essentially solving simultaneous equations from vector components, not requiring any excluded concept like momentum.

parts.reason: M8.4 covers equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces with forces resolved in 2 dimensions.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: Continuation of the same equilibrium-of-particle problem covered by M8.4.

parts.label: c

parts.reason: Further application of equilibrium under coplanar forces (M8.4), solving simultaneous trig-based force equations.
